reasons: narrow: The previous claim used an ambiguous phrase, every queried HSIC value, for both coverage and singleton recovery. Exact-path separation is sufficient to retain the true oracle execution and hence gives honest graph-set coverage without width conditions, but it does not separate labels on other compatible paths. Singleton recovery therefore needs the stronger all-compatible-query separation promise in addition to the score and HSIC width inequalities. The replacement also records the already-proved score-radius bound, direct margins, sufficient sample-size order, dimension-seven elbow, and no-minimax qualification.

verdict.note: Accepted: the proof correctly separates exact-path HSIC separation for no-width graph-set coverage from all-compatible-query separation for singleton recovery, and it establishes the stated 4d/vbar score-radius bound, direct margins, sufficient rates, and d=7 elbow without hidden assumptions or class overtransfer.
